stem: Draw the graphical form of the function $f$ where $f(x) = -x^2 + 6x - 11$ in the interval $[0, 6]$. Sketch the curve with your finger across the whole interval; then, from your drawing, find the solution set of the equation $x^2 - 6x + 11 = 0$.
solution: Draw a smooth curve through them; it opens downward with its highest point at (3, -2), below the x-axis.
The curve does not meet the x-axis.
$x^2-6x+11=0$ is the same equation as $-x^2+6x-11=0$, so it has no real roots.

hints.text: A function gives one value of f(x) for each x. Draw one smooth curve from left to right without doubling back.
The table runs over the whole interval given. Your curve should start at its left end and reach its right end.
Check the value f(x) at a few x-values in your table and make sure your curve passes through those heights.
Look at the sign of the x² coefficient in f(x): it decides whether the curve opens upward or downward.
Make a table of values for x from the left end of the interval to the right end, plot the points, then join them smoothly.

notes: Freehand quadratic on [0,6]; grid y -12..0 holds all values (max -2). Solution set ∅ is read from the curve not meeting the x-axis.
